heroHeadline: Russia Launches 216+ Drones After Ceasefire Expires — Kyiv Kindergarten and Residential Building Hit
heroSubtitle: Hours after the Trump-brokered 72-hour ceasefire (May 9–11) expired without extension, Russia launched a massive 216+ drone attack against Ukraine on May 12. In Kyiv's Obolon district, debris from a downed drone hit the roof of a 16-storey residential building and sparked a fire; a separate drone struck a kindergarten roof and shattered windows in a neighboring apartment block. Dnipro transport infrastructure was hit (1 injured); Cherkasy region sustained 2 wounded; Mykolaiv's energy infrastructure was struck, causing blackouts; Kherson reported a woman wounded. Over 80 aerial bombs and 30+ airstrikes were recorded across the country. With the ceasefire collapsed and no extension agreed, multiple outlets and analysts declared the trilateral US-Ukraine-Russia peace process effectively 'dead.' ISW's May 11 assessment confirmed Russia suffered a net territorial loss of 45 square miles in April 2026 — its first net loss since August 2024 — and has failed to recruit soldiers as fast as it loses them for six consecutive months. Ukraine is scaling up domestic weapons and drone production to prepare for a protracted conflict.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OHCHR, ISW, CSIS, Ukrainian MoD, US DoD, NATO, IAEA, EU Council, UK MoD, and major news outlets including Reuters, BBC, AP, Al Jazeera, Bloomberg, Kyiv Independent, Ukrinform, Euronews, NPR, CBC, RTE, and RBC-Ukraine. Casualty figures are estimates; Russia has never released official figures.
